Graph.title: JSON Graph Visualizer
Graph.description: Visualize your JSON data as an interactive node graph. Explore object and array hierarchies at a glance, switch between horizontal and vertical layouts, and understand data relationships intuitively.
Graph.metaTitle: JSON Graph Visualizer Online - Interactive Node Graph | JSONKit
Graph.metaDescription: Free online JSON graph visualizer. Visualize JSON as an interactive node graph with automatic hierarchical layout. Switch between horizontal and vertical views.

seoContent.heading: What is a JSON Graph Visualizer?
seoContent.paragraph: A JSON graph visualizer renders JSON data as an interactive node graph, making it easy to explore complex hierarchical structures. JSONKit's graph tool supports both horizontal and vertical layouts with automatic node positioning, helping you understand object and array relationships at a glance.
howTo: Paste your JSON into the input editor.
The graph is generated automatically, with each object and array shown as a node.
Switch between horizontal and vertical layouts to fit the shape of your data.
Zoom and pan to explore large structures.
features: Interactive node graph of objects, arrays and their values.
Automatic hierarchical layout powered by the ELK layout engine.
Horizontal and vertical layout options.
Zoom, pan and fit-to-screen controls.
Rendered entirely in your browser.

faq.q: When is a graph more useful than a tree?
faq.a: A graph shows the whole structure at once, which makes it easier to explain a data model to teammates or to spot unexpected nesting. A tree is better for drilling into one specific branch.

faq.q: Can it handle large JSON files?
faq.a: Yes, but very large documents produce very large graphs. For files with thousands of nodes, the tree viewer or a JSONPath query is often the faster way to find specific data.

faq.q: Is my data uploaded to generate the graph?
faq.a: No. The layout is computed in your browser, and your JSON is never sent to a server.

Beautify.title: JSON Beautifier & Minifier
Beautify.description: Format and pretty-print your JSON data to make it easier to read, or minify it to reduce file size without changing the data.
Beautify.metaTitle: JSON Beautifier & Minifier Online - Format JSON | JSONKit
Beautify.metaDescription: Free online JSON beautifier and minifier. Pretty-print JSON with proper indentation or compress it to save space. Fast, client-side processing with no data upload.

seoContent.heading: What is a JSON Beautifier?
seoContent.paragraph: A JSON beautifier (also known as JSON formatter or JSON pretty-printer) takes raw, compact JSON data and formats it with proper indentation, line breaks, and spacing to make it human-readable. JSONKit's beautifier processes everything in your browser — your data never leaves your device. You can also minify JSON to remove whitespace, reducing file size for production use.
howTo: Paste or type your JSON into the input editor on the left.
Click Beautify to pretty-print it with 2-space indentation, or Minify to strip all unnecessary whitespace.
Review the result in the output editor. If the input is not valid JSON, an error message tells you what went wrong.
Copy the result to your clipboard with one click.
features: Pretty-print JSON with consistent indentation and line breaks.
Minify JSON into a single line to reduce payload size.
Syntax highlighting, code folding and bracket matching powered by the Monaco editor (the editor used in VS Code).
Handles large documents quickly because everything runs locally in your browser.
No sign-up, no upload: your data never leaves your device.

faq.q: Does beautifying or minifying change my data?
faq.a: No. Both operations only change whitespace. Keys, values, and the order of properties stay exactly the same, so the formatted and minified versions are equivalent JSON.

faq.q: Is my JSON sent to a server?
faq.a: No. JSONKit parses and formats the JSON with JavaScript running in your browser. Nothing is uploaded, which makes it safe to use with API responses or configuration that contain internal data.

faq.q: Why do I get an "Invalid JSON" error?
faq.a: The beautifier requires strictly valid JSON. Common causes are trailing commas, single-quoted strings, unquoted keys and comments. Use the JSON Repair tool to fix these automatically, or the JSON Validator to find the exact line of the error.

faq.q: When should I minify JSON?
faq.a: Minify JSON when size matters more than readability, for example when embedding JSON in a URL or HTML attribute, storing it in a database column, or sending it over the network. Keep the beautified version for code reviews and debugging.

Validate.title: JSON Validator
Validate.description: Validate your JSON strings against the standard. Find syntax errors quickly with precise line numbers and error messages.
Validate.metaTitle: JSON Validator Online - Syntax Checker with Line Numbers | JSONKit
Validate.metaDescription: Free online JSON validator and syntax checker. Detect errors with precise line numbers and detailed error messages. Validate JSON instantly in your browser.

seoContent.heading: What is a JSON Validator?
seoContent.paragraph: A JSON validator checks your JSON data against the official JSON specification (RFC 8259) to detect syntax errors. JSONKit's validator provides precise line numbers and descriptive error messages so you can quickly locate and fix issues like missing commas, unclosed brackets, or invalid escape sequences.
howTo: Paste the JSON you want to check into the editor.
Click Validate JSON.
If the JSON is valid, you will see a confirmation. If not, the error message shows the line and the reason, such as an unexpected token or a missing comma.
Fix the reported problem and validate again until the document passes.
features: Strict validation against the JSON specification (RFC 8259).
Precise error messages with line numbers to locate problems fast.
Detects common mistakes such as trailing commas, single quotes, unquoted keys and unclosed brackets.
Runs entirely in your browser, so private data stays on your machine.

faq.q: What is the difference between JSON validation and JSON Schema validation?
faq.a: This validator checks syntax: whether the text is well-formed JSON. JSON Schema validation goes further and checks whether the data has the expected structure, such as required fields and value types. Use the JSON Schema Validator for that.

faq.q: Why is JSON with comments reported as invalid?
faq.a: Standard JSON does not allow comments. Formats like JSONC or JSON5 do, but most parsers and APIs reject them. The JSON Repair tool can strip comments and fix other non-standard syntax for you.

faq.q: Can I validate very large files?
faq.a: Yes. Validation happens locally, so the limit is your browser's memory rather than an upload size. Documents of several megabytes validate in well under a second on a modern computer.

Viewer.title: JSON Tree Viewer
Viewer.description: Visualize your JSON data as an interactive tree. Expand, collapse, and explore complex nested structures effortlessly.
Viewer.metaTitle: JSON Tree Viewer Online - Interactive JSON Explorer | JSONKit
Viewer.metaDescription: Free online JSON tree viewer. Visualize JSON as an interactive, collapsible tree structure. Explore nested objects and arrays with JSONPath copy support.
Viewer.enterValid: Enter valid JSON to view tree

seoContent.heading: What is a JSON Tree Viewer?
seoContent.paragraph: A JSON tree viewer renders JSON data as an interactive, hierarchical tree structure. You can expand and collapse nodes to explore deeply nested objects and arrays. JSONKit's tree viewer supports JSONPath copying, type-based color coding, and auto-expands the first two levels for quick overview.
howTo: Paste your JSON into the input panel.
The tree view on the right updates automatically as soon as the JSON is valid.
Click the arrows next to objects and arrays to expand or collapse them.
Hover over any node and click the copy icon to copy its JSONPath, then use it in the JSONPath Query tool.
features: Interactive, collapsible tree for objects and arrays.
Shows the type of each value and the number of items in every object and array.
Makes deeply nested API responses easy to navigate.
Copy the JSONPath of any node with one click.
Updates live as you edit the input.

faq.q: When is a tree view better than formatted text?
faq.a: For large or deeply nested JSON, a tree lets you collapse the parts you do not care about and focus on one branch. Formatted text is better when you need to copy or edit the raw document.

faq.q: Can I see my JSON as a diagram instead?
faq.a: Yes. The JSON Graph Visualizer renders the same data as a node graph, which is useful for understanding relationships between objects at a glance.

faq.q: Is there a size limit?
faq.a: There is no fixed limit. Very large documents with tens of thousands of nodes may render more slowly, so collapse branches you are not inspecting.

Compare.title: JSON Diff & Compare
Compare.description: Compare two JSON objects side-by-side to see differences. Visual highlighting makes it easy to spot added, removed, or modified values.
Compare.metaTitle: JSON Diff & Compare Tool - Side-by-Side Comparison | JSONKit
Compare.metaDescription: Free online JSON diff and compare tool. Compare two JSON objects side-by-side with visual highlighting of added, removed, and modified values.
Compare.instruction: Edit directly in the left (Original) and right (Modified) panels to compare.

seoContent.heading: What is a JSON Diff Tool?
seoContent.paragraph: A JSON diff tool compares two JSON documents and highlights the differences between them. JSONKit's diff tool offers side-by-side and inline views powered by Monaco Editor's diff engine, with color-coded additions, deletions, and modifications. Perfect for debugging API responses, config changes, or data migrations.
howTo: Paste the original JSON into the left panel.
Paste the modified JSON into the right panel.
Differences are highlighted immediately: added lines, removed lines and changed values are marked in different colors.
Switch between split view and inline view, and edit either side directly to see the diff update.
features: Side-by-side and inline diff views.
Line-level and character-level highlighting of changes.
Edit both documents in place with full syntax highlighting.
Useful for comparing API responses, configuration versions and test fixtures.
Both documents stay in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

faq.q: Does the order of keys matter when comparing?
faq.a: The diff compares the text of the two documents, so reordered keys show up as changes. For the cleanest comparison, format both sides the same way first, for example with the JSON Beautifier.

faq.q: Can I compare two API responses?
faq.a: Yes. Copy each response into one side of the editor. This is a quick way to see what changed between two environments, two API versions, or before and after a code change.

faq.q: Is it safe to compare confidential data?
faq.a: Yes. The comparison runs entirely in your browser, and neither document is sent to a server.

Convert.title: JSON Converter
Convert.description: Convert JSON data to other popular formats like YAML, XML, and CSV. You can also convert these formats back to JSON.
Convert.metaTitle: JSON Converter - JSON to YAML, XML, CSV & Back | JSONKit
Convert.metaDescription: Free online JSON converter. Convert JSON to YAML, XML, CSV and back. Bidirectional conversion with instant preview. No server upload required.

seoContent.heading: What is a JSON Converter?
seoContent.paragraph: A JSON converter transforms JSON data to and from other popular data formats. JSONKit supports bidirectional conversion between JSON and YAML, XML, and CSV. The conversion happens instantly in your browser with live preview, making it ideal for data migration, API testing, and format interoperability.
howTo: Choose the target format: YAML, XML or CSV.
Paste your JSON into the input editor; the converted output appears in the output editor.
Click Swap to reverse the direction and convert YAML, XML or CSV back into JSON.
Copy the result.
features: Two-way conversion between JSON and YAML, XML and CSV.
CSV conversion turns an array of objects into rows, using the object keys as column headers.
Great for moving data between configuration files, spreadsheets and APIs.
Conversion runs locally in your browser.

faq.q: What JSON structure works best for CSV?
faq.a: An array of flat objects with the same keys, for example [{"name":"Alice","age":30},{"name":"Bob","age":25}]. Each object becomes a row and each key becomes a column. Deeply nested objects do not map naturally to a table.

faq.q: Is JSON to YAML conversion lossless?
faq.a: For standard JSON data, yes. YAML is a superset of JSON, so objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null all convert cleanly. YAML-only features such as anchors and comments have no JSON equivalent when converting back.

faq.q: Why would I convert JSON to XML?
faq.a: Some older systems, SOAP services and enterprise integrations still expect XML. Converting lets you reuse JSON data with those systems without writing a custom script.

Type.title: JSON to Code Converter
Type.description: Generate type definitions and class structures for TypeScript, Go, Python, and more from your JSON data.
Type.metaTitle: JSON to Code - Generate Types & Interfaces Online | JSONKit
Type.metaDescription: Free online JSON to Code converter. Generate TypeScript, Go, Python, C#, Rust, Swift, Java, C++, and Kotlin code from JSON with instant, secure client-side generation.

seoContent.heading: Convert JSON to Code Instantly
seoContent.paragraph: Stop manually writing type definitions. JSONKit's JSON to Code tool automatically generates type-safe interfaces, structs, and classes for various programming languages including TypeScript, Go, Python, C#, and more. Just paste your JSON and get ready-to-use code instantly.
howTo: Paste a representative JSON sample, such as a real API response, into the input editor.
Choose the target language and enter a name for the root type.
Click Generate.
Copy the generated types or classes into your project.
features: Generates code for TypeScript, Go, Python, C#, Rust, Swift, Java, C++ and Kotlin.
Infers nested types, arrays and optional fields from the sample.
Powered by quicktype, a widely used open-source type generator.
Saves time when integrating a new API or third-party data source.

faq.q: How accurate are the generated types?
faq.a: Types are inferred from the sample you provide. If a field can be null or missing, include an example of that in the sample so the generator marks it as optional. Review the result just as you would hand-written code.

faq.q: Is my JSON sent to a server?
faq.a: Yes, this is the one JSONKit tool that uses a server: the sample is sent to generate the code and the result is returned immediately. The input is not logged or stored. Avoid pasting secrets; a sample with dummy values works just as well.

faq.q: Should I use generated TypeScript interfaces for runtime validation?
faq.a: Interfaces only exist at compile time. If you also need to validate data at runtime, combine them with a JSON Schema and the JSON Schema Validator, or a runtime validation library.

typescript.title: JSON to TypeScript Converter
typescript.description: Paste JSON and get TypeScript interfaces for every nested object, ready to drop into your project.
typescript.metaTitle: JSON to TypeScript Converter - Generate Interfaces Online | JSONKit
typescript.metaDescription: Convert JSON to TypeScript interfaces online. Paste an API response and get typed interfaces for nested objects and arrays, ready to copy into your .ts files.

seoContent.heading: Generate TypeScript interfaces from JSON
seoContent.paragraph: Typing API responses by hand is slow and easy to get wrong. This converter reads a JSON sample and produces one exported interface per object shape: nested objects become their own named interfaces, arrays become typed arrays such as string[], and numbers, strings and booleans map to number, string and boolean. The output contains only type declarations, with no runtime code, so it adds nothing to your bundle.
howTo: Paste a real response from the API you are integrating, for example from your browser's network tab.
Set the type name to what the root object represents, such as User or ApiResponse.
Copy the interfaces into a types.ts file and annotate your fetch result, for example const user: User = await res.json().

faq.q: Does it generate interfaces or type aliases?
faq.a: It generates exported interfaces. For typing API data they behave the same as object type aliases, and you can rename or convert them freely after copying.

faq.q: How do I get optional properties (field?: string)?
faq.a: The generator only knows what the sample shows. Put several objects in an array where some of them omit the field, and that property is generated as optional. A field that is always null in the sample is typed as null, so give it a real value if you know its type.

faq.q: Do the interfaces validate data at runtime?
faq.a: No. TypeScript types are erased at compile time, so a malformed response will not throw. If you need runtime checks, generate a JSON Schema with the JSON Schema tool and validate against it, or use a validation library.

go.title: JSON to Go Struct Converter
go.description: Turn JSON into Go structs with json tags, plus Unmarshal and Marshal helpers for encoding/json.
go.metaTitle: JSON to Go Struct Converter - Generate Structs with JSON Tags | JSONKit
go.metaDescription: Convert JSON to Go structs online. Get exported fields with json tags, nested struct types and encoding/json helpers, ready to paste into your package.

seoContent.heading: Generate Go structs with json tags from JSON
seoContent.paragraph: Go needs a struct for every JSON object you want to decode, and every field needs a json tag when the key does not match the Go name. This converter writes those structs for you: snake_case keys such as allowed_origins become exported fields such as AllowedOrigins with the matching json tag, nested objects become separate struct types, whole numbers become int64 and decimals float64. It also adds an Unmarshal function and a Marshal method built on the standard encoding/json package, so there are no third-party dependencies.
howTo: Paste a JSON sample, such as a config file or an API response.
Enter the root struct name, for example ServerConfig.
Copy the code into a .go file, change package main to your own package name, and decode with json.Unmarshal or the generated Unmarshal function.

faq.q: Why are numbers generated as int64 instead of int?
faq.a: JSON has no size limit for integers, so int64 is the safe choice on every platform. You can change a field to int after copying if you know the value range.

faq.q: How do I add omitempty to the json tags?
faq.a: The generator writes plain tags that match the keys in your sample. Add ,omitempty by hand to fields that should be left out when empty during Marshal; decoding works the same either way.

faq.q: How are nullable or missing fields handled?
faq.a: If the sample shows a field as null, or missing in some array items, it is generated as a pointer type such as *string, so you can tell an absent value from an empty one.

python.title: JSON to Python Class Converter
python.description: Generate typed Python classes from JSON, with from_dict and to_dict methods for parsing and serializing.
python.metaTitle: JSON to Python Class Converter - Generate Typed Classes Online | JSONKit
python.metaDescription: Convert JSON to Python classes with type hints. Get one class per object plus from_dict and to_dict helpers, using only the standard library.

seoContent.heading: Generate typed Python classes from JSON
seoContent.paragraph: json.loads gives you nested dicts, so typos in keys only show up at runtime and your editor cannot autocomplete anything. This converter produces a class for each object in your JSON, with type-annotated attributes (str, int, float, bool, List[...]), a from_dict static method that checks each value's type while parsing, and a to_dict method for turning the object back into a dict for JSON. It uses only the typing module from the standard library.
howTo: Paste a JSON sample, for example a webhook payload or an API response.
Name the root class, for example Order.
Save the code as a module and parse data with Order.from_dict(json.loads(text)); call to_dict() before json.dumps when sending it back.

faq.q: Are these dataclasses or Pydantic models?
faq.a: Neither. They are plain classes with type hints and explicit from_dict/to_dict methods, so they need no third-party packages. You can add @dataclass or port the fields to Pydantic if your project already uses it.

faq.q: What happens if the data does not match the types?
faq.a: The generated helper functions use assert isinstance checks, so from_dict raises an AssertionError when a value has an unexpected type. Note that asserts are skipped when Python runs with -O.

faq.q: Which Python version is required?
faq.a: The code uses annotations from the typing module and works on Python 3.7 and later.

csharp.title: JSON to C# Class Converter
csharp.description: Generate C# classes with properties and JsonProperty attributes from JSON, ready for Newtonsoft.Json.
csharp.metaTitle: JSON to C# Class Converter - Generate POCO Classes Online | JSONKit
csharp.metaDescription: Convert JSON to C# classes online. Get PascalCase properties with JsonProperty attributes, nested classes and FromJson/ToJson helpers for Newtonsoft.Json.

seoContent.heading: Generate C# classes from JSON
seoContent.paragraph: Deserializing JSON in .NET starts with a model class whose properties match the payload. This converter writes those classes for you: camelCase keys become PascalCase properties with a [JsonProperty] attribute holding the original key, nested objects become their own partial classes, arrays become typed arrays, whole numbers become long and decimals double. It also adds a static FromJson method and a ToJson extension method with converter settings for Newtonsoft.Json (Json.NET).
howTo: Paste a JSON sample, such as a response from the API your service calls.
Enter the root class name, for example Product.
Install the Newtonsoft.Json NuGet package, add the file to your project, rename the QuickType namespace to your own, and call Product.FromJson(json).

faq.q: Does it work with System.Text.Json?
faq.a: The attributes and helpers target Newtonsoft.Json. For System.Text.Json, keep the properties, replace [JsonProperty] with [JsonPropertyName] from System.Text.Json.Serialization, and deserialize with JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Product>(json).

faq.q: Why are numbers generated as long and double?
faq.a: JSON numbers have no fixed size, so long and double avoid overflow surprises. Change them to int or decimal after copying if your domain needs it, for example decimal for money.

faq.q: Why are the classes declared as partial?
faq.a: Partial classes let the generated properties and the FromJson helper live in separate declarations, and let you add your own members in another file without editing the generated one.

rust.title: JSON to Rust Struct Converter
rust.description: Generate Rust structs that derive serde's Serialize and Deserialize from a JSON sample.
rust.metaTitle: JSON to Rust Struct Converter - Generate Serde Structs Online | JSONKit
rust.metaDescription: Convert JSON to Rust structs with serde derives. Get typed fields for nested objects and arrays, ready for serde_json::from_str.

seoContent.heading: Generate serde structs from JSON
seoContent.paragraph: In Rust, the usual way to read JSON is to deserialize it into structs with serde and serde_json. This converter writes those structs from a sample: each object becomes a struct with #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)], nested objects get their own struct, arrays become Vec<T>, whole numbers become i64, decimals f64 and strings String. Field names are kept in snake_case, and a #[serde(rename = "...")] attribute is added when a JSON key is not a valid snake_case identifier.
howTo: Paste a JSON sample, such as an event payload or a config file.
Enter the root struct name, for example Event.
Add serde (with the derive feature) and serde_json to Cargo.toml, paste the structs into a module, and parse with serde_json::from_str::<Event>(&text).

faq.q: Why are the fields private?
faq.a: The generator leaves fields without pub, which is enough for serde inside the module. Add pub to the fields you need to read from other modules.

faq.q: How are optional fields represented?
faq.a: If a field is null or missing in some of the sample items, it is generated as Option<T>, so serde accepts both cases. Fields that are always present get plain types, and a missing one is a deserialization error.

faq.q: Which crates do I need?
faq.a: Add serde with features = ["derive"] and serde_json. The comment at the top of the output also shows the older extern crate style, which current Rust editions do not need.

swift.title: JSON to Swift Codable Converter
swift.description: Generate Swift structs conforming to Codable from JSON, with convenience initializers for decoding.
swift.metaTitle: JSON to Swift Converter - Generate Codable Structs Online | JSONKit
swift.metaDescription: Convert JSON to Swift Codable structs online. Get immutable structs, nested types, CodingKeys and convenience initializers that decode from Data, String or URL.

seoContent.heading: Generate Swift Codable structs from JSON
seoContent.paragraph: Codable is the standard way to decode JSON in Swift, but writing the model structs for a large payload is tedious. This converter generates a struct conforming to Codable for each object, with let properties typed as Int, Double, String, Bool, nested structs and arrays. It adds a CodingKeys enum when a JSON key differs from the Swift property name, plus extensions with initializers that decode from Data, a JSON String or a URL, a with(...) method for making modified copies, and jsonData()/jsonString() for encoding back.
howTo: Paste a JSON sample, such as the response your iOS or macOS app receives.
Enter the root type name, for example Article.
Add the file to your Xcode project and decode with try Article(jsonString) or JSONDecoder().decode(Article.self, from: data).

faq.q: Does it work with SwiftUI and URLSession?
faq.a: Yes. The structs are plain Codable value types, so you can decode the Data returned by URLSession and pass the result to SwiftUI views like any other model.

faq.q: How are snake_case keys handled?
faq.a: Properties get Swift-style camelCase names (is_featured becomes isFeatured), and a CodingKeys enum maps each one to the original JSON key, so you do not need to set keyDecodingStrategy.

faq.q: Can I remove the convenience extensions?
faq.a: Yes. Only the struct declarations and CodingKeys are needed for Codable. The extensions and the newJSONDecoder/newJSONEncoder helpers are optional conveniences you can delete.

java.title: JSON to Java Class Converter
java.description: Generate Java classes with getters and setters from JSON, plus a Jackson-based Converter.
java.metaTitle: JSON to Java Class Converter - Generate POJOs with Jackson | JSONKit
java.metaDescription: Convert JSON to Java classes online. Get POJOs with getters, setters and Jackson annotations, plus a Converter class for reading and writing JSON.

seoContent.heading: Generate Java POJOs from JSON
seoContent.paragraph: Mapping JSON in Java usually means writing a POJO for every object, with private fields, getters, setters and annotations. This converter generates them from a sample: each object becomes a class with Jackson @JsonProperty annotations on its accessors, nested objects become separate classes, arrays become typed arrays, and whole numbers become long. A Converter class with fromJsonString and toJsonString methods wraps the Jackson ObjectMapper setup, including date and time parsing helpers.
howTo: Paste a JSON sample, for example a REST response your Spring or Android app consumes.
Enter the root class name, for example Customer.
Add jackson-databind to your Maven or Gradle build, move each class into its own .java file in your package, and call Converter.fromJsonString(json).

faq.q: Why is the output so long?
faq.a: Java needs explicit fields, getters and setters, and the generated Converter includes date-time helpers for the java.time API. If you only need the models, copy the data classes and use your existing ObjectMapper.

faq.q: Can I use Java records or Lombok instead?
faq.a: The generator writes classic classes for maximum compatibility. You can convert them to records (Java 16+) or annotate them with Lombok's @Data after copying; Jackson supports both.

faq.q: Does it work with Spring Boot?
faq.a: Yes. Spring Boot uses Jackson by default, so the annotated classes can be used directly as @RequestBody or response types without the Converter class.

cpp.title: JSON to C++ Converter
cpp.description: Generate C++ classes with nlohmann/json serialization functions from a JSON sample.
cpp.metaTitle: JSON to C++ Converter - Generate Classes for nlohmann/json | JSONKit
cpp.metaDescription: Convert JSON to C++ classes online. Get classes with getters and setters plus from_json/to_json functions for the nlohmann/json library.

seoContent.heading: Generate C++ classes from JSON for nlohmann/json
seoContent.paragraph: C++ has no built-in JSON support, and the popular nlohmann/json library needs a from_json and to_json function for every type it converts automatically. This converter writes a header that declares a class per object, with private members, getters and setters, and the matching from_json/to_json functions, so json.get<SensorReading>() and assigning an object back to json just work. Whole numbers become int64_t, decimals double and strings std::string.
howTo: Paste a JSON sample, such as a device message or a config file.
Enter the root class name, for example SensorReading.
Save the output as a header, add json.hpp from nlohmann/json to your include path, and parse with nlohmann::json::parse(text).get<quicktype::SensorReading>().

faq.q: Which libraries does the generated code need?
faq.a: It needs the single-header nlohmann/json library (json.hpp). The header also includes boost/optional.hpp, which is used for optional fields; if your JSON has no optional fields you can remove that include.

faq.q: Which C++ standard is required?
faq.a: nlohmann/json requires C++11 or later. Apart from the libraries above, the generated header uses only standard library types.

faq.q: Can I change the quicktype namespace?
faq.a: Yes. Rename namespace quicktype to your own; from_json and to_json are found by argument-dependent lookup as long as they stay in the same namespace as the classes.

kotlin.title: JSON to Kotlin Data Class Converter
kotlin.description: Generate Kotlin data classes from JSON, with toJson and fromJson helpers.
kotlin.metaTitle: JSON to Kotlin Converter - Generate Data Classes Online | JSONKit
kotlin.metaDescription: Convert JSON to Kotlin data classes online. Get immutable val properties, nested classes, List types and fromJson/toJson helpers for Android and JVM projects.

seoContent.heading: Generate Kotlin data classes from JSON
seoContent.paragraph: Kotlin data classes are the natural model type for JSON on Android and the JVM. This converter produces one data class per object with immutable val properties: whole numbers become Long, decimals Double, arrays List<T> and nested objects their own data class. The generated code uses the Klaxon library and adds a toJson method and a companion fromJson function, so a single call turns a JSON string into a typed object.
howTo: Paste a JSON sample, for example the response your Android app receives.
Enter the root class name, for example Movie.
Add the Klaxon dependency, paste the classes into a .kt file in your package, and call Movie.fromJson(jsonString).

faq.q: Can I use these classes with kotlinx.serialization, Moshi or Gson?
faq.a: Yes. The data class declarations are plain Kotlin. Remove the Klaxon helpers and add your library's annotation, such as @Serializable for kotlinx.serialization, to each class.

faq.q: How are nullable fields generated?
faq.a: Fields that are null or missing in part of the sample become nullable types such as String?, so Kotlin's null safety makes you handle them.

faq.q: Why Long instead of Int?
faq.a: JSON integers have no size limit, so Long avoids overflow. Change a property to Int if you know the values are small, for example a year or a count.

Query.title: JSONPath Query
Query.description: Extract data from JSON using JSONPath expressions. Query nested objects and arrays with powerful path syntax.
Query.metaTitle: JSONPath Query Tool - Extract Data from JSON | JSONKit
Query.metaDescription: Free online JSONPath query tool. Extract data from JSON using powerful JSONPath expressions. Query nested objects and arrays with instant results.

seoContent.heading: What is JSONPath Query?
seoContent.paragraph: JSONPath is a query language for JSON, similar to XPath for XML. It lets you extract specific data from complex JSON structures using path expressions like $.store.book[*].author. JSONKit's query tool supports the full JSONPath specification with instant results, match counting, and built-in example queries to get you started.
howTo: Paste your JSON into the input editor.
Type a JSONPath expression, such as $.store.book[*].author, into the query field.
Click Execute to see every matching value and the number of matches.
Use the Examples menu to try common patterns like filters and recursive search.
features: Full JSONPath support, including wildcards, array slices, recursive descent (..) and filter expressions.
Shows the number of matches together with the results.
Built-in examples to learn the syntax quickly.
Runs in your browser with no data upload.

faq.q: What is JSONPath?
faq.a: JSONPath is a query language for JSON, similar to XPath for XML. An expression starts at the root ($) and walks through keys and array indexes to select one or more values.

faq.q: How do I filter an array by a value?
faq.a: Use a filter expression. For example, $.store.book[?(@.price < 10)] selects every book whose price is below 10, and $..book[?(@.isbn)] selects books that have an isbn field.

faq.q: How do I find a key anywhere in the document?
faq.a: Use recursive descent with two dots. For example, $..author returns every author value no matter how deeply it is nested.

Escape.title: JSON Escape & Unescape
Escape.description: Escape JSON strings for embedding in other JSON or code, or unescape previously escaped JSON strings back to their original format.
Escape.metaDescription: Free online JSON escape and unescape tool. Escape JSON strings for embedding in code or unescape them back to original format. Fast, browser-based processing.

seoContent.heading: What is JSON Escape & Unescape?
seoContent.paragraph: JSON escaping converts special characters in strings (like quotes, backslashes, and newlines) into escape sequences so they can be safely embedded in JSON or source code. Unescaping reverses this process. JSONKit handles both directions instantly, useful when working with nested JSON strings or embedding JSON in code.
howTo: Paste the text or JSON you want to process into the input editor.
Click Escape to turn it into a JSON string literal, with quotes, backslashes and line breaks escaped.
Click Unescape to turn an escaped string back into readable JSON.
Copy the result into your code, configuration file or API request.
features: Escapes double quotes, backslashes, newlines, tabs and other control characters.
Unescapes strings copied from logs, databases or nested JSON fields.
Useful for embedding JSON inside another JSON value, an environment variable or source code.
Processing happens locally in your browser.

faq.q: Why do I need to escape JSON?
faq.a: When JSON is stored as a string inside another JSON document or a programming language string, its quotes and backslashes would end the string early. Escaping prefixes them with backslashes so the outer document stays valid.

faq.q: My log shows JSON full of \" characters. How do I read it?
faq.a: That JSON was escaped, often more than once. Paste it into the input and click Unescape. If the result still contains escaped quotes, unescape it again.

faq.q: Is escaping the same as URL encoding?
faq.a: No. JSON escaping uses backslash sequences such as \" and \n, while URL encoding uses percent sequences such as %22. Use the method that matches where the text will be placed.

Repair.title: JSON Repair
Repair.description: Automatically fix malformed JSON. Repairs common issues like trailing commas, missing quotes, single quotes, and comments.
Repair.metaTitle: JSON Repair Tool - Fix Malformed JSON | JSONKit
Repair.metaDescription: Free online JSON repair tool. Automatically fix malformed JSON including trailing commas, missing quotes, single quotes, comments, and unquoted keys.

supports.trailingCommas: Trailing commas in arrays and objects
supports.singleQuotes: Single quotes instead of double quotes

seoContent.heading: What is JSON Repair?
seoContent.paragraph: JSON repair automatically fixes common syntax errors in malformed JSON, such as trailing commas, missing or mismatched quotes, single quotes instead of double quotes, JavaScript-style comments, and unquoted property keys. JSONKit's repair tool can often recover data from broken JSON that standard parsers reject.
howTo: Paste the broken JSON into the input editor.
Click Repair.
Review the repaired, valid JSON in the output editor. If the input was already valid, you will be told so.
Copy the result or continue working with it in the other tools.
features: Removes trailing commas and JavaScript-style comments.
Adds missing quotes around keys and converts single quotes to double quotes.
Fixes common issues in JSON copied from JavaScript code, logs or LLM output.
Runs entirely in your browser.

faq.q: What kinds of errors can be repaired?
faq.a: Trailing commas, comments, single-quoted strings, unquoted property names and similar mistakes that are common when JSON is written by hand or copied from JavaScript. Severely truncated or ambiguous input may not be recoverable.

faq.q: Can repair change the meaning of my data?
faq.a: The repair only fixes syntax, but when the input is ambiguous it has to make a best guess. Always review the result before using it in production.

faq.q: Why does JSON from an AI model or a log fail to parse?
faq.a: Output from language models and log lines often contains comments, trailing commas, single quotes or text cut off mid-way. Running it through JSON Repair is usually the fastest way to make it parseable.

Schema.title: JSON Schema Validator
Schema.description: Validate your JSON data against a JSON Schema. Ensure your data conforms to a defined structure with detailed error reporting.
Schema.metaDescription: Free online JSON Schema validator. Validate JSON data against JSON Schema definitions with detailed error reporting. Supports draft-07 and later.
Schema.enterDataAndSchema: Enter JSON data and schema, then click Validate

seoContent.heading: What is JSON Schema Validation?
seoContent.paragraph: JSON Schema is a vocabulary for defining the structure, content, and semantics of JSON data. A JSON Schema validator checks whether your data conforms to a given schema definition. JSONKit uses the Ajv library for fast, spec-compliant validation with detailed error messages pointing to exact locations of violations.
howTo: Paste your JSON data into the data editor, or click Load Example to start with a sample.
Paste the JSON Schema that describes the expected structure into the schema editor.
Click Validate.
Read the list of errors. Each one shows where in the data the problem is and which schema rule failed.
features: Validation powered by Ajv, one of the most widely used JSON Schema validators.
Supports JSON Schema draft-07, including common formats such as email, date-time, uri and uuid.
Reports all errors at once instead of stopping at the first one.
Data and schema stay in your browser.

faq.q: What is JSON Schema?
faq.a: JSON Schema is a vocabulary for describing the structure of JSON data: which properties are required, what type each value must be, allowed ranges, string patterns and more. It is widely used for API contracts and configuration validation.

faq.q: Which JSON Schema version is supported?
faq.a: The validator uses the draft-07 specification, which is compatible with most schemas in use today, including those generated by many tools and the OpenAPI ecosystem.

faq.q: Why does my data fail with "must have required property"?
faq.a: The schema lists that property under required, but it is missing from the data. Either add the property to the data or remove it from the required array in the schema.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.metaDescription: JSONKit privacy policy. Learn how we handle your data: almost every tool runs in your browser, and JSON to Code sends your sample to our server only to generate code, without logging or storing it.

dataCollection.title: Data Collection
dataCollection.content: JSONKit does not collect or store your JSON data. Almost every tool runs entirely in your browser: the JSON you paste is parsed, formatted, validated, converted and compared on your own device and is never sent anywhere. The one exception is JSON to Code, which sends your JSON sample to our server to generate type definitions and returns the result immediately; the input is not logged or stored.

localStorage.title: Local Storage
localStorage.content: We use browser local storage to save your preferences (such as theme settings) and to remember your last input for convenience. This data is stored only on your device and is never sent to our servers.

cookies.title: Cookies and Third-Party Services
cookies.content: We use the following third-party services that may set cookies:
cookies.googleAdsense: Google AdSense: Used to display advertisements. Google may use cookies to personalize ads based on your browsing history.
cookies.vercelAnalytics: Vercel Analytics: Used to understand how visitors use our site. Vercel Analytics does not use cookies and collects no personal data.

thirdParty.title: Third-Party Links
thirdParty.content: Our website may contain links to third-party websites. We are not responsible for the privacy practices of these external sites. We encourage you to read the privacy policies of any linked websites you visit.

contact.title: Contact Us
contact.content: If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us through our GitHub repository.

About.title: About JSONKit
About.metaTitle: About JSONKit - Free Online JSON Toolkit
About.metaDescription: Learn about JSONKit, a free and open-source collection of JSON tools for developers: who builds it, how your data is handled, and how the project is funded.
About.intro: JSONKit is a free, open-source collection of online JSON tools for developers. It brings formatting, validation, comparison, conversion, querying and code generation together in one fast, ad-light interface, so you do not have to jump between a dozen different sites.

mission.title: Why JSONKit exists
mission.content: JSON is everywhere: API responses, configuration files, logs and databases. Most online JSON tools do just one thing, are cluttered with pop-ups, or quietly upload your data to a server. JSONKit was built to be the single bookmark a developer needs for everyday JSON work — quick to load, keyboard friendly, available in five languages, and respectful of your data.

privacy.title: How your data is handled
privacy.content: Almost every tool on JSONKit runs entirely in your browser: the JSON you paste is parsed, formatted, validated and compared on your own device and is never sent anywhere. The one exception is JSON to Code, which sends your JSON sample to our server to generate type definitions and returns the result immediately; the input is not logged or stored. See the Privacy Policy for details about cookies and analytics.

maintainer.title: Who builds it
maintainer.content: JSONKit is designed, built and maintained by Ktaewon, an independent software developer who works with JSON APIs every day. Bug reports, feature ideas and translation fixes from users directly shape what gets built next.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.content: The complete source code is available on GitHub under the MIT license. You can read exactly how each tool works, report issues, suggest improvements or open a pull request.

funding.title: How JSONKit stays free
funding.content: All tools are free to use with no account required. Hosting and development costs are covered by a small number of non-intrusive advertisements. Ads never have access to the JSON you work with.

Contact.title: Contact
Contact.metaTitle: Contact JSONKit - Bug Reports & Feature Requests
Contact.metaDescription: Contact the JSONKit maintainer. Report bugs, request new JSON tools or features, and ask questions through GitHub.
Contact.intro: JSONKit is maintained in the open on GitHub. The fastest way to reach the maintainer — whether you found a bug, want a new feature, or spotted a translation error — is to open an issue.

issues.title: Report a bug or request a feature
issues.content: Open a GitHub issue describing what happened or what you would like to see. Issues are public, so other users can follow progress and add their own feedback.

repo.title: Source code
repo.content: Browse the source, read the changelog, or contribute a fix directly with a pull request. Contributions of all sizes are welcome.

tips.bug: For bugs, include the tool you were using, your browser, and the steps to reproduce the problem.
tips.feature: For feature requests, describe the task you are trying to accomplish, not only the solution you have in mind.
tips.privacy: Never paste confidential data, API keys or personal information into a public issue. A small anonymized sample is enough.

Contact.responseTime: Issues are usually reviewed within a few days.
